question.summary: The universal correctable-code lower bound scales as n/e^4, while a simple worst-case upper bound scales as n/e. The gap is not closed.
question.importance: The function c(e,n) gives the code dimension guaranteed against an arbitrary e-dimensional error space. Closing the gap would establish the worst-case rate available without assuming a noise model.
question.unresolved: Determine the exact asymptotics of c(e,n), or give matching lower bounds and explicit worst-case error models.

claims.title: A structure-free lower bound is proved
claims.text: Knill, Laflamme and Viola show c(e,n) is greater than n divided by e squared times e squared plus one. No matching construction is known.

decisions.rationale: Status assessed against the archived statement in the 2026-08-12 primary-source audit; the evidence ledger lists the results considered.

editorial.interpretation: The correct denominator is e^2(e^2+1), not e^2(e+1).
